arguments.name: drag_gap
arguments.description: local push minus fitted current push: a drop means extra drag (rudder snag, weed) or a sudden current change

arguments.message: boat slower than pod power predicts: check rudder snag or current
shaft power still well above critical power after the start
pod reserve low with far to go

arguments.condition: elapsed_s > 300 and shaft_power_w < 0.85 * cp_shaft_w and remaining_m > 1000
arguments.message: shaft power well below critical power: easing too much or pod fault

tool_calls.name: take_note
tool_calls.text: Plan (min 1): 10 km, out-and-back 1250 m legs. Even effort near critical power: shaft ~185-190 W (cp_shaft 182), boat ~126 W. Hard start normal; let it settle by min 3. Save reserve for final 1-1.5 km sprint. Watches: drag_jump (drag_gap=push_local-push_along < -0.25, rudder snag?), over_cp_after_start, pod_reserve_low, effort_sag. CP may be 10-25 pct off: check pod vs boat reserve agreement later.

text: no cue: hard start is normal at minute 1; set plan note and watches for drag, over-pacing, low reserve and effort sag

arguments.text: Min 4 (800 m): settled. Shaft 189 W vs sustainable 186 (pod reserve 61 pct, fine). Boat model disagrees: boat power 138 vs CP 126, boat reserve 45 pct, says too fast. Boat gets more W per shaft W than in test (0.73 vs 0.69) and push_local ~+0.1. Trusting pod for effort for now; recheck whether boat reserve keeps diverging (boat CP may be low).

text: no cue: effort settled at critical power per the pod; boat-speed reserve disagrees, noted to recheck

arguments.text: Min 7 (1.4 km): shaft steady 190 W (sustainable 186), pod reserve 52 pct draining ~2.5 pct/min; boat reserve 25 pct draining ~6 pct/min. Both models put paddler ~4-6 pct above CP. Asked paddler: 3/10, all good, plenty. Suspect test CP is LOW (maybe 10-20 pct). Plan: hold effort, no push yet; test: if boat reserve sits near 0 for 4+ min with no fade (fade_pct > -2), raise CP (boat ~ steady power) and then lift effort a few W. Re-ask paddler ~min 13 to see if effort rating climbs.

arguments.message: boat reserve read empty for 4 min: check fade; no fade means CP is higher than the test

text: no cue: effort steady near sustainable per pod; paddler says 3/10, suspect CP low, gathering evidence before pushing

arguments.text: Min 10 (2.0 km): paddler crept up to shaft 196 W on own; pod reserve 41 pct (empties in 1.7 km at this power if pod CP right). Boat reserve hit 0 at min 9 but NO fade (fade +0.3, speed 3.29 steady) -> boat model CP/W too low. Paddler 4/10 plenty (was 3/10 at min 7). Decision point: when pod reserve ~15-20 pct (approx min 14-16), if no fade and effort <=6/10, raise cp_shaft (~200-205) and cp boat (~140). If fade appears or effort jumps to 8+, ease to ~182 W.

arguments.message: pod reserve under 18 pct: decide whether CP is higher (no fade) or ease

text: no cue: paddler steady with no fade and says 4/10; letting the pod reserve test whether CP is higher before changing effort
